title: Honest Interval Length for CATE Variance at the Homogeneity Null
banked_reason: D0.5.G: tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling=7 < ceiling_for_field=7.4; mathematics and cited-source verification pass; no within-scope field-tier repair.
gap_reasons: Its significance remains confined to one quadratic functional under known scalar uniform design and common smoothness envelopes, rather than a broadly applicable inference framework.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 delivered an informal matched finite-honesty null expected-length frontier for arbitrary nonnegative finite-moment outcomes, with the same order when propensity is supplied. D0.5 mathematics passed after the classical moment bound was source-attested, but the projected paper score 7.0 remained below the field threshold 7.4; an independent main validity gate confirmed downgrade without an in-scope repair. No formalization stages or Lean certification were run; positioning/editorial caveats remain preserved, and a broader inference framework would require a new research anchor.
tldr: Homogeneous conditional mean treatment effects place \(V\) at a boundary where regular normal inference degenerates. The target is a sharp all-smoothness, all-moment worst-null expected-length frontier for connected intervals with at least \(0.90\) coverage at each finite sample size throughout the original nonnegative conditional-moment parent, together with its same-record supplied-propensity comparison. Selection and prognosis remain unknown. Combined raw contrasts require a directly proved conditional \(L_\nu\) contraction, independent nuisance-risk integration and normalized complete-record lower mixtures. The conditional moment envelope is a newly maintained model restriction. Piecewise rate calculations serve as falsifiable handles; rates, critical logarithms, saturation and the oracle-preservation region are research outputs.
gap: The nearest true-variance inference result, \cite{SanchezBecerra2023RobustVCATE}, separates uniform asymptotic coverage of a prediction-dependent target from pointwise true-target coverage. The existing finite-moment bank settles global squared risk at one moment order. Neither settles the stipulated full-parent finite-sample null expected-length objective.
fill: Prove the raw conditional \(L_\nu\) contraction directly, integrate every nuisance-risk and interval-length realization, and establish matching nonnegative complete-record mixtures for each candidate branch. The robust block-median theorem is a methodological donor, not a theorem about \(T\). Determine all public parameter regimes and the oracle-information boundary on the identical parent and record budget.
